title: Delhi Police considered reporter jackets, press IDs to distinguish journalists from ‘reel-makers’ during anti-SIR protests

ai.summary: Delhi Police considered issuing reporter vests and IDs to distinguish journalists from 'reel-makers' during anti-SIR protests in October, but the plan didn't materialize due to concerns about replication and confusion.

facts.claim: Delhi Police considered issuing high-visibility reporter vests carrying its name and separate identification cards to journalists covering the anti-SIR protests in the Capital in October
facts.quote: The Delhi Police had considered issuing high-visibility reporter vests carrying its name and separate identification cards to journalists covering the anti-SIR protests in the Capital in October, in an attempt to distinguish genuine mediapersons from those it described as ‘reel-makers’, senior police officers told The Hindu.

facts.claim: The proposals did not materialise, with officers concerned that the vests and identification cards could be easily replicated
facts.quote: The proposals, however, did not materialise, with officers concerned that the vests and identification cards could be easily replicated, potentially creating another layer of confusion during an already tense law-and-order situation.

facts.claim: Police officers cited circulation of fake press identification cards and instances of protesters claiming to be independent journalists to avoid detention
facts.quote: They cited the circulation of fake press identification cards, the absence of a clear mechanism to authenticate journalists and instances of protesters claiming to be independent journalists to avoid detention.

facts.claim: The police argued that social media content creators, ‘reel-makers’ and people carrying cameras or microphones could not automatically be considered bona fide journalists
facts.quote: the police’s November 16 affidavit before the Supreme Court, in which it argued that social media content creators, ‘reel-makers’ and people carrying cameras or microphones could not automatically be considered bona fide journalists or claim the protections available to accredited mediapersons.

ai.background_note: Delhi Police faced challenges distinguishing journalists from social media content creators during anti-SIR protests in October 2026, leading to confusion and potential misdetentions.
